clues.narrowing: Rules out coastal and single-river towns; puts the player where three rivers meet in a wide northern land.

source.quote: Three major rivers meet within Ottawa, making it an important trade and travel area for thousands of years.

clues.text: This city sits where three rivers meet, in the east of a wide northern land. Thick woods once ringed it, far from the sea.

clues.narrowing: Rules out mild-winter capitals; keeps places with polar winters and hot, wet summers.

source.quote: Outbreaks of polar air often cause frigid temperatures.

clues.text: Winters bite hard here, when polar air drops the cold far below freezing. Summers flip the tale, with hot wet air and heat waves in July.

clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to the lumber town a queen chose as capital in 1857.

source.quote: The Queen sent a letter to colonial authorities selecting Ottawa as the capital, effective 31 December 1857.

clues.text: In 1857 a queen chose this far off lumber town as the new capital. Its deep woods and lone spot helped it please both halves of the land.

clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: in winter its canal freezes into the world's largest skating rink, right through the city.

source.quote: the section of the Rideau Canal passing through central Ottawa has been re-purposed as what is officially the world's largest and second longest skating rink.

clues.text: In winter, the canal through this city freezes into the world's largest skating rink. Folks skate on the thick ice for mile after mile, right through town.

clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the national parliament, top court, and prime minister all work in this city.

source.quote: these include the Parliament of Canada, the Supreme Court, the residence of Canada's viceroy, and the Office of the Prime Minister.

clues.text: The parliament of Canada writes the laws of the land in this city. The prime minister and the top court work here too.

reveal.blurb: Workers built a lumber town here in 1826, by a new canal that linked rivers and lakes. In 1857 a queen chose it as the capital, and parliament soon met on the hill. Boats still climb its old canal locks today. Ottawa is the capital of Canada.
